_comment: SYNTHETIC EXAMPLE - no real customer. Reference intake for sow_type=infrastructure_build. Shows current-state / target-state architecture sections with a service mapping table, a phase/deliverable timeline, and a pre-discovery estimate range rather than a fixed price.

document.title: AWS to Google Cloud Platform Replication
document.subtitle: Marketplace Listing Readiness

stakeholders.name: Nadia Okonkwo
stakeholders.title: Head of Platform Engineering
stakeholders.description: Technical point of contact; architecture decisions and approvals

team.description: Commercial ownership, engagement governance and customer communication
Solution architecture, platform design, Terraform adaptation and technical delivery

background.objective:
Ravensbourne Analytics Ltd. operates a B2B analytics platform currently deployed on AWS. To list the platform on a cloud marketplace, Ravensbourne requires a functioning infrastructure presence on Google Cloud.

This engagement is **not** a migration off AWS. Ravensbourne will continue to operate and serve existing customers there. The objective is to **replicate** the AWS architecture on Google Cloud as a greenfield deployment, adapting the existing Terraform codebase to GCP-native services, so that an initial set of pilot customers can be onboarded on Google Cloud.

Partner will act as a hands-on technical extension of Ravensbourne's engineering team, providing the infrastructure and platform engineering effort the in-house team does not currently have bandwidth for.

current_state.intro: The production environment runs on Amazon EKS with cluster autoscaling and progressive delivery. Traffic is routed through Route 53 and an Application Load Balancer to a set of containerised services. Infrastructure is defined in Terraform across the application repositories.

layers.components: RDS PostgreSQL, S3 (artifacts and analytics exports)
SSO via external IdP, AWS Secrets Manager

notes.label: Being retired independently of this project
notes.text: The legacy batch scheduler. Not part of the Google Cloud parity scope.

target_state.intro: The Google Cloud deployment mirrors the AWS topology component-for-component wherever a direct equivalent exists, minimising application-level changes and maximising reuse of the existing Terraform.

mapping.to: Cloud DNS + HTTPS Load Balancer + Cloud Armor
mapping.notes: Cloud Armor adds WAF-equivalent protection at the edge
Node pools re-mapped from EKS node groups
Schema replicated by Partner; pilot tenant data imported from customer-provided exports
Phase 1 via the S3 interoperability API, avoiding an application refactor
Replaces IRSA directly rather than stepping down to static keys

mapping.to: Cloud Monitoring, Cloud Logging + Grafana / Sentry
mapping.notes: Parity dashboards rebuilt on GCP-native telemetry

sections.heading: Network Design
sections.body: Private GKE clusters with Private Service Connect for Cloud SQL and Cloud Storage, preserving the existing trust-zone security model.

service_sections.heading: Landing Zone & Networking
bullets: Validate the existing Google Cloud organisation, billing and committed spend setup.
Provision dedicated Google Cloud projects for production and development.
Design and provision VPC, subnets and Private Service Connect for Cloud SQL and Cloud Storage.
Establish the IAM baseline and configure GKE Workload Identity Federation.

service_sections.heading: Compute Platform (GKE)
bullets: Provision private GKE cluster(s) mirroring the EKS topology.
Configure node pools for baseline services and batch workloads.
Port Kubernetes manifests and Helm charts from EKS to GKE, adjusting for GCP-specific ingress, storage classes and annotations.

service_sections.heading: Data Layer Replication
bullets: Provision Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL and migrate the existing schema.
Provision Cloud Storage buckets configured for the S3 interoperability API and Uniform Bucket-Level Access.
Import pilot tenant data from customer-provided exports.

service_sections.heading: Observability, Security & Secrets Management
bullets: Configure Secret Manager for database credentials and API keys.
Build Cloud Monitoring and Grafana dashboards for parity with the existing setup.
Configure Cloud Armor policies at the load balancer.

service_sections.heading: CI/CD & Infrastructure-as-Code Adaptation
bullets: Convert and extend Terraform modules from AWS to GCP providers.
Configure a versioned Cloud Storage bucket for Terraform remote state.
Configure Artifact Registry and adapt the CI pipeline for GCP-hosted builds.

service_sections.heading: Validation & Handover
bullets: End-to-end smoke testing of GKE services and the data layer.
Deliver runbook and architecture documentation for the Google Cloud environment.
Conduct knowledge transfer session(s) with the engineering team.

out_of_scope_extra: Full migration or decommissioning of the AWS environment. AWS remains live for existing customers.
Marketplace listing documentation, submission and approval, which is handled directly by the marketplace operator.
Global load balancing and full multi-region routing. Single-region only in this phase.
Data migration beyond the initial pilot tenants.

timeline.note: Estimated overall duration: four (4) to six (6) weeks from kickoff, contingent on timely access to the information described in the Dependencies section.

phases.activities: Validate projects and billing; confirm scale from AWS billing data; finalise network design; configure Workload Identity Federation
phases.deliverable: Landing zone provisioned; confirmed scope document

phases.activities: Stand up GKE cluster and node pools; provision Cloud SQL and Cloud Storage; convert Terraform; wire CI/CD
phases.deliverable: GKE environment running core services in development

phases.activities: Migrate schema and import pilot tenant data; validate integrity
Configure Secret Manager, Cloud Armor and monitoring parity; run end-to-end smoke tests

phases.deliverable: Final architecture and runbook documentation; sign-off

prerequisites_before: Provide Partner with access to the Google Cloud organisation, billing account and in-scope projects.
Provide AWS billing and usage exports sufficient to validate scale assumptions.
Provide architecture diagrams and the AWS configuration detail required for replication.
Identify the pilot customer tenants in scope for data import.
prerequisites_ongoing: Ensure timely availability of the technical point of contact for architecture questions and reviews.
Provide review and written approval at each phase boundary.
Promptly communicate any organisational, technical or scope changes affecting delivery.
assumptions: The existing Terraform codebase is well-structured and can be adapted to Google Cloud with minimal refactoring.
Scope is limited to the production and development environments.
Initial data migration covers only the pilot customer tenants, not the full customer base.

risks.risk: An incomplete AWS resource inventory delays accurate scoping
risks.mitigation: Confirm scale via AWS billing export and architecture diagram review during Phase 1.

risks.risk: S3 to Cloud Storage interoperability gaps require application-level changes
risks.mitigation: Validate interoperability early against a sandbox bucket before full replication.

success_criteria: **Functional Parity** - Core platform services run on GKE with functional parity to the AWS deployment.
**Data Layer Readiness** - Cloud SQL and Cloud Storage are provisioned, populated with pilot tenant data, and validated for integrity.
**Operational Readiness** - The engineering team can observe, deploy and troubleshoot the Google Cloud environment using documented runbooks.
change_management: Any change to the scope, timeline or cost described in this SOW must be agreed in writing by both Parties before related work begins.

pricing.payment_terms: This estimate excludes ongoing Google Cloud consumption and hosting costs, which are billed directly under the Customer's own Google Cloud account.
